hmrc.name: HMRC
hmrc.how: Call 0300 200 3300 or write. Final tax return may be needed for year of death.

dwp.name: DWP / State pension
dwp.how: Call 0800 731 0469. Stop pension payments and claim any arrears.

probate.name: Probate Registry
probate.how: Apply online at gov.uk for Grant of Probate. Allow 4-8 weeks.

nhs-gp.name: NHS / GP surgery
nhs-gp.how: Contact the GP surgery directly to cancel NHS records and return unused medications.

council-tax.name: Council tax
council-tax.how: Contact the local council to update or cancel the council tax account.

electoral.name: Electoral register
electoral.how: Contact the local council to remove from the electoral register.

dvla.name: DVLA
dvla.how: Return driving licence and notify about any vehicles. gov.uk/tell-dvla-about-bereavement

passport.name: HM Passport Office
passport.how: Cancel and return the passport by post to HM Passport Office, Newport, NP20 9AR.

energy.name: Energy supplier
energy.how: Contact provider to take final meter readings and close or transfer the account.

broadband.name: Broadband / phone
broadband.how: Contact provider to cancel or transfer contract. Early exit fees may be waived on death.

water.name: Water company
water.how: Contact local water company to update account name or close if property is empty.

royal-mail.name: Royal Mail redirect
royal-mail.how: Set up mail redirection at royalmail.com to avoid missing important correspondence.

subscriptions.name: Subscriptions & direct debits
subscriptions.how: Cancel all standing orders via the bank. Check accounts list for known subscriptions.

life-insurance.name: Life insurance
life-insurance.how: Contact insurer with policy number. Life policies are usually paid outside probate.

pension-private.name: Private pension provider
pension-private.how: Contact each provider. Pensions written in trust are paid to nominated beneficiaries.

resources.title: Help & Guides

items.label: What is a trusted person?
items.detail: A trusted person on Everstead is someone the plan owner has chosen to share part or all of their estate plan with. Depending on your role, you may be an executor, next of kin, financial power of attorney holder, or simply a trusted family member.

items.label: What does an executor do?
items.detail: An executor is legally responsible for administering the estate after death. This includes locating the will, applying for probate, notifying institutions, settling debts, and distributing assets. Everstead gives you the information you need to do this, it does not replace legal advice for complex estates.

items.label: What does a power of attorney holder do?
items.detail: If you hold a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) for property and financial affairs, you can act on behalf of the plan owner if they lose mental capacity. This is a serious legal responsibility. Only act within the scope of the LPA and keep records of all decisions.

items.label: Your access level
items.detail: You can only see what the plan owner has explicitly shared with you. Some people see the full plan; others see only specific sections. If you need access to something not shown here, contact the plan owner directly.

items.label: Finding the will
items.detail: Look in the Documents section. If the original is held by a solicitor, the document record should include their contact details. You will need the original signed will (not a scan) to apply for probate in England and Wales.

items.label: Locating the LPA
items.detail: The LPA must be registered with the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) before it can be used. The registration certificate will show the OPG reference number. Financial institutions will ask to see a certified copy.

items.label: Downloading documents
items.detail: Use the Download button next to any document to save a copy. Store these securely, you may need to send certified copies to banks, insurers, and HMRC.

items.label: What to do if documents are missing
items.detail: If you cannot find a key document here, check with the plan owner's solicitor, bank, or family members. For a missing will, the Certainty National Will Register can run a search. For lost LPAs, contact the OPG directly.

items.label: Notifying financial institutions
items.detail: Each bank, insurer, and pension provider must be notified separately. Most accept a death certificate and grant of probate. Use the Tell Us Once service (gov.uk) to notify multiple government departments in a single step.

items.label: Freezing and closing accounts
items.detail: Accounts are typically frozen on notification of death. Joint accounts may transfer automatically to the surviving holder. Sole accounts require probate before funds can be released.

items.label: Pensions and life insurance
items.detail: These are usually written in trust and paid outside of probate, check the nomination of beneficiary forms. Contact the provider directly with the policy number shown in the Accounts section.

items.label: Subscriptions and direct debits
items.detail: Cancel ongoing subscriptions as quickly as possible to avoid charges. Check the Subscriptions section for a list. Contact each provider with proof of death.

items.label: Tax and final returns
items.detail: A final income tax return may be required for the year of death. If the estate exceeds the inheritance tax threshold (currently £325,000 + any allowances), an IHT400 form must be filed with HMRC before probate.

items.label: Co-executors
items.detail: If there are multiple executors, all must act together unless one formally steps aside. Decisions should be agreed in writing where possible. Disagreements between executors can delay probate significantly.

items.label: Beneficiaries
items.detail: You are not obliged to share the details of the estate with beneficiaries during administration, only the final distribution. However, keeping them reasonably informed reduces disputes.

items.label: Solicitors and professionals
items.detail: For complex estates, instruct a probate solicitor early. Look in the People section for the plan owner's nominated solicitor. Most estate solicitors charge a percentage of the estate value or an hourly rate.

items.label: When to seek legal advice
items.detail: Always seek legal advice if: the estate includes a business, overseas assets, disputed property, estranged family members, or debts that exceed the estate's value.

practical.title: Practical steps when the time comes

items.label: Register the death
items.detail: In England and Wales, a death must be registered within 5 days at a local register office. You will receive a death certificate, request at least 10 certified copies, as institutions will ask for originals.

items.label: Locate the will and contact solicitors
items.detail: Do this before making any major financial decisions. The will may name specific funeral wishes, executors, and bequests that affect immediate next steps.

items.label: Apply for probate
items.detail: If the estate requires it, apply to the Probate Registry for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there is no will). This typically takes 4-8 weeks. Estates under £10,000 may not require probate.

items.label: Notify Everstead via this dashboard
items.detail: Use the Report a Death button in the left panel to formally notify Everstead. This will trigger a verification process and, once confirmed, release any personal messages addressed to you.

reportDeath.title: Report a death
reportDeath.subtitle: Notify Everstead that {{name}} has passed away
reportDeath.intro: We are deeply sorry for your loss. This process allows you to formally notify Everstead of the passing of {{name}}. Once verified by our team:
bullets: The subscription will enter a 30-day wind-down period, no further charges will be taken.
Delegate access to this plan will remain active for 90 days to allow proper handoff.
Data will be securely archived and then deleted in accordance with our retention policy.
You will receive a confirmation email and reference number within 2 business days.
reportDeath.notice: This form is for notifications only. Everstead is not a legal service. Please also contact relevant authorities, financial institutions, and legal professionals as required.
reportDeath.certPlaceholder: Leave blank if not yet obtained
reportDeath.uploadLead: Upload a copy of the death certificate or coroner's letter
reportDeath.notesPlaceholder: Any additional context for the Everstead team…
reportDeath.consent: I confirm that I am an authorised delegate on this Everstead plan, that the information provided is accurate to the best of my knowledge, and that I have the right to notify Everstead of the death of the plan owner. I understand that Everstead will verify this report before taking any action on the account.
reportDeath.submittedBody: We have received your notification. The Everstead team will review and verify the information within 2 business days. The plan owner's subscription will be placed in a 30-day wind-down period, after which the account will be closed and data securely handled in accordance with our retention policy.

bullets: Your report will be reviewed by the Everstead team within 2 business days.

firstSteps.deceasedSubtitle: A prioritised checklist for the days ahead
firstSteps.incapSubtitle: As attorney, here's where to start

deceasedSteps.label: Register the death
deceasedSteps.detail: Within 5 days at a local register office. Request at least 10 certified death certificates, banks and institutions each need an original.

deceasedSteps.label: Locate the will
deceasedSteps.detail: Check the Documents tab. The original signed will (not a scan) is needed for probate. Check with their solicitor if it's not here.

deceasedSteps.label: Notify close family
deceasedSteps.detail: Inform immediate family before making any formal notifications to institutions.

deceasedSteps.label: Apply for probate
deceasedSteps.detail: A Grant of Probate from the Probate Registry is usually needed to access accounts. Takes 4-8 weeks. Estates under ~£10,000 may not require it.

deceasedSteps.label: Notify financial institutions
deceasedSteps.detail: Check the Accounts tab for a full list. Use Tell Us Once (gov.uk) for government departments. Settld.com can notify banks and utilities in bulk.

deceasedSteps.label: Cancel subscriptions
deceasedSteps.detail: Use the accounts list to find and cancel ongoing direct debits, they continue to charge until cancelled.

incapSteps.label: Confirm your LPA is registered
incapSteps.detail: A Lasting Power of Attorney must be registered with the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) before you can use it. Check you have the registration certificate.

incapSteps.label: Review the documents
incapSteps.detail: Check the Documents tab for the LPA certificate, any medical directives, and care instructions.

incapSteps.label: Contact the plan owner's bank
incapSteps.detail: Present your registered LPA to gain access to their accounts. Each institution has its own process, call ahead to find out what they need.

incapSteps.label: Review the instructions
incapSteps.detail: Check the Instructions tab for any guidance the plan owner left for this situation.

incapSteps.label: Keep a record of all decisions
incapSteps.detail: As attorney, you must act in the donor's best interests and keep records. Note all decisions and reasons.
